messages:
Marta: quick RFC follow-up — we hit a flaky case with the local-repo proxy + operator TTL when doing tiered activation. wondering if we should change the activation handshake semantics or just bump TTLs. short summary: proxy evicted seed blobs during a churn window and operator interpreted missing blobs as a failed activation, rolled back, then retried, causing churn.

Tyler: can you paste the minimal sequence you saw?

Marta: sure. sequence: 1) node pulls compact index from proxy; 2) proxy GC evicts a seldom-used seed blob; 3) operator apply starts, fails on manifest verify; 4) operator sets state=failed and reduces TTL to expedite cleanup; 5) proxy rehydrate later, operator retries and hits a mismatch -> loop.

Deepa: oof. two obvious levers: make apply idempotent to tolerate transient missing blobs, or make proxy eviction respect in-flight activation leases.

Samir: +1 to in-flight leases. if proxy honored a per-activation lease header, GC could skip blobs referenced by active manifests. cheaper than doubling all TTLs.

Nina: what about operator-side: keep a soft-failure state that triggers background fetch from alt sources for N seconds instead of immediate rollback? avoids flip-flop.

Marta: here was our temp workaround: bump operator.activation_ttl to 10m and set proxy.min_reserve to 2 replica copies. fewer churns but increases disk usage.

Tyler: does the operator already surface the manifest->blob dependency list to the proxy during preflight? if not we need a small API change: 
```http
POST /v1/locks/activation 
Content-Type: application/json
{ "cluster": "cluster-7", "manifest": "sha256:abcd...", "deadline": 1680000000 }
```
Proxy returns 200 and GC skips marked blob ids until deadline.

Deepa: API looks fine. tradeoffs: 1) increases coordination complexity (distributed lease table), 2) requires durable cleanup if operator crashes. we'd need a lease-heartbeat and operator reclaim policy.

Samir: also consider signed-lease tokens that expire — proxy can evict based on time without central state. operator signs a short-lived lease (JWT-like) that enumerates referenced blobs.

Nina: signed lease could be replayed though. add nonce + audit log? but for air-gapped, we might not want full PKI churn.

Marta: another angle: make activation two-phase: PREPARE (fetch & pin blobs to local store) then ACTIVATE (swap pointers). PREPARE would surface all fetch errors and only complete when pinned. ACTIVATE is then cheap and atomic.

Tyler: that's nice — reduces time-in-flight for manifests that reference missing blobs. downside: extra disk usage during PREPARE and longer prep time.

Deepa: plus operator needs quota bookkeeping for PREPARE space. but it gives a clean rollback: if PREPARE fails, we never touch running state.

Samir: +1. For air-gapped clusters, PREPARE should prefer local-proxy first, then a fallback mirror (USB or local registry). we should expose fallback order in the operator config.

Nina: metrics we need: prep_duration, prep_failures_by_reason (missing-blob, verify-fail, liveness), lease_renewals, gc_evictions_prevented. that will help tune TTLs.

Marta: agreed. proposed action items:
- implement PREPARE/ACTIVATE state machine in operator (default PREPARE timeout 5m)
- add lease header support to proxy (signed-lease prototype)
- expose fallback mirror list in operator config
- add metrics + alert (prep_fail_rate > 1% over 15m)

Tyler: small nit: PREPARE should do streaming verify (verify chunks as they arrive) so we can fail fast on corrupt content. code sketch: 
```bash
# pseudo
fetch(manifest) -> for blob in manifest.blobs: stream_verify(blob) -> pin(blob)
if any verify fails -> abort PREPARE and delete pinned partials
```

Deepa: also consider a GC backoff hook: when GC sees a lease header, it decrements an internal priority counter. if many leases reference a blob, it bumps retention. helps with high churn.

Samir: question on operator reclaim: if operator crashes mid-PREPARE, who cleans up leases? maybe lease keys include operator-id and a TTL; proxy will auto-expire. operator on restart will reconcile by scanning local pinned blobs and re-advertise leases.

Marta: sounds good. I'll sketch RFC PR with diagrams and options: A) TTL bump only (current workaround), B) signed-lease + proxy GC skip, C) PREPARE/ACTIVATE + fallback mirrors. recommend C + signed-lease as guardrail.

Nina: recommend we run a small canary in staging with PREPARE enabled but short timeout to measure increased disk pressure. also add a tooling script to evict pinned content to simulate GC.

ops-bot: deploy-notice: rolling canary with operator PREPARE feature flagged will be scheduled tomorrow 09:00 UTC to staging clusters. :rocket:

Tyler: awesome. one last thought: document operator API changes clearly for private/on-prem customers — they often want minimal network calls, so provide an opt-out (ttl-only) fallback.

Marta: yep, RFC will include compatibility notes and a migration path. thanks all :heart:
